title: "Image information and input size selection"

Date: 13/7/2026

## GOHREP

**Goal:**

1. Measure how much information (Shannon entropy) each cropped CDA image keeps
   as it is shrunk to smaller and smaller sizes. This justifies one standard
   input size for model training.
2. Describe how Shannon entropy, the balance of green to red, and the mean green
   level of a CDA relate to its severity score.

**Hypothesis:**

1. Shannon entropy stays about the same from the raw crop down to a moderate
   size. It then falls once the image is too small to hold the same range of
   pixel values. A size just above that drop keeps almost all the information
   with the fewest pixels, and so the least training compute.
2. Under UV light, healthy tissue fluoresces red, and cell death shifts the
   colour towards green. So the green to red ratio and the mean green level
   should both rise with severity score. Shannon entropy alone should overlap
   heavily between scores.

**Rationale:**

Shrinking an image reduces its number of pixels. That limits how many distinct
values it can hold, which caps its Shannon entropy. If entropy holds down to a
given size, that size still carries the information a model could use. Shrinking
further loses information. Finding the size at which entropy starts to fall
gives an information-based reason for the 64 × 64 px input size used elsewhere in
this project (see `07_visual_complexity`).

This analysis repeats, for the whole dataset, figures first made for Set 1 alone
in the Year 1 probationary review.

## 1. Setup

#| output: false
# 1.1
library(tiff)
suppressMessages(library(EBImage)) # image resizing
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(patchwork)
library(here)
library(RColorBrewer)
```

### 1.2 Helper functions and colour palettes

```{r}
# 1.2
source(here("src", "plotting_helpers.R"))

save_plot <- make_save_plot("09_image_entropy")
```

### 1.3 Configuration and metric functions

```{r}
# 1.3
# Cropped CDA images are stored one folder per median severity score (0-6);
# the folder name is the score. Each image is resized to a range of square
# side lengths and its Shannon entropy computed at every size. "Raw" is the
# original crop (variable native size, see 07_visual_complexity).
data_dir <- here("data", "cropped_images_medoid")
sizes <- c(128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4)
size_levels <- c("Raw", as.character(sizes)) # x-axis order: large -> small

# Shannon entropy of an image, replicating the default behaviour of
# skimage.measure.shannon_entropy used in the original Year 1 analysis:
# histogram every value in the array (flattened across the RGB channels) as an
# 8-bit intensity, then H = -sum(p_i * log2(p_i)). More distinct, evenly used
# intensities -> higher entropy; the maximum is 8 bits.
shannon_entropy <- function(arr) {
  v <- as.integer(round(pmin(pmax(arr, 0), 1) * 255))
  counts <- tabulate(v + 1L, nbins = 256L)
  p <- counts[counts > 0] / length(v)
  -sum(p * log2(p))
}

# Per-image metrics: entropy at every side length, plus two colour metrics
# computed on the raw crop over non-dark pixels (max(R,G,B) >= 0.1, which
# excludes the black background and holes in the leaf, as in the original).
#   - log_gr: log of the green:red pixel-count ratio. Under this imaging
#     healthy tissue is red and cell death shifts towards green, so this is
#     expected to rise with score. A +1 pseudocount avoids log(0).
#   - mean_green: mean green-channel intensity (0-255) of the non-dark pixels.
image_metrics <- function(path) {
  img <- readTIFF(path, info = FALSE)
  if (length(dim(img)) == 2) img <- array(img, dim = c(dim(img), 3))
  img <- img[, , 1:3, drop = FALSE]

  ent <- c(Raw = shannon_entropy(img))
  for (s in sizes) {
    r <- pmin(pmax(EBImage::resize(img, w = s, h = s), 0), 1)
    ent[as.character(s)] <- shannon_entropy(r)
  }

  R <- img[, , 1]
  G <- img[, , 2]
  B <- img[, , 3]

  # Non-dark pixels (drops black background/holes) for the colour metrics.
  nondark <- pmax(R, G, B) >= 0.1
  n_red <- sum(R[nondark] > G[nondark])
  n_green <- sum(G[nondark] >= R[nondark])

  # Per-pixel brightness and two leaf-region definitions (see 5.5):
  #  - otsu_*: an image-adaptive two-class threshold (Otsu, from the image's
  #    own brightness histogram). It cleanly removes a dark background but, in
  #    high-score CDAs, tends to select the bright lesion rather than the whole
  #    leaf, so it is used only to illustrate that difficulty.
  #  - leaf_*: a low fixed cut that removes only the near-black background,
  #    keeping all tissue - a less score-dependent lighting proxy.
  bright_px <- (R + G + B) / 3
  thr <- EBImage::otsu(bright_px, range = c(0, 1))
  otsu_mask <- bright_px > thr
  if (sum(otsu_mask) < 0.02 * length(otsu_mask)) otsu_mask <- bright_px >= 0.1
  leaf_mask <- bright_px >= 0.10

  c(ent,
    log_gr = log((n_green + 1) / (n_red + 1)),
    mean_green = mean(G[nondark]) * 255,
    otsu_frac = mean(otsu_mask),
    otsu_bright = mean(bright_px[otsu_mask]) * 255,
    leaf_frac = mean(leaf_mask),
    leaf_bright = mean(bright_px[leaf_mask]) * 255
  )
}
```

---

## 2. Compute per-image metrics

The dataset has a few thousand crops, each resized six times. So the metrics
for each image are computed once and saved in `entropy_cache/`. Delete that file
to compute them again.

```{r}
# 2.1
cache_path <- here("analyses", "09_image_entropy", "entropy_cache", "cda_metrics.rds")

if (file.exists(cache_path)) {
  metrics <- readRDS(cache_path)
} else {
  scores <- list.dirs(data_dir, recursive = FALSE, full.names = FALSE)
  scores <- scores[grepl("^[0-9]+$", scores)]

  rows <- list()
  for (sc in scores) {
    files <- list.files(file.path(data_dir, sc),
      pattern = "\\.tif$",
      full.names = TRUE
    )
    for (f in files) {
      m <- image_metrics(f)
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- tibble::tibble(
        image_id = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f)),
        score = as.integer(sc),
        size = size_levels,
        entropy = as.numeric(m[size_levels]),
        log_gr = unname(m["log_gr"]),
        mean_green = unname(m["mean_green"]),
        otsu_frac = unname(m["otsu_frac"]),
        otsu_bright = unname(m["otsu_bright"]),
        leaf_frac = unname(m["leaf_frac"]),
        leaf_bright = unname(m["leaf_bright"])
      )
    }
    message(sprintf("score %s: %d images", sc, length(files)))
  }
  metrics <- dplyr::bind_rows(rows)
  saveRDS(metrics, cache_path)
}

# Long form (one row per image x size) for the size plots, and a per-image
# table (one row per image) for the score/colour plots.
metrics <- metrics %>%
  mutate(
    size = factor(size, levels = size_levels),
    score_f = factor(score, levels = 0:6)
  )

per_image <- metrics %>%
  filter(size == "Raw") %>%
  transmute(image_id, score, score_f,
    entropy_raw = entropy, log_gr, mean_green,
    otsu_frac, otsu_bright, leaf_frac, leaf_bright
  )

cat(sprintf(
  "Loaded metrics for %d CDA images across %d scores.\n",
  dplyr::n_distinct(metrics$image_id), dplyr::n_distinct(metrics$score)
))
per_image %>%
  count(score, name = "n") %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

## 3. Image information versus input size

First, a summary of the original sizes of the cropped CDA images. CDAScorer
stores each CDA as a square crop, whose side length depends on the size of the
bounding box. The minimum, median, maximum, mean and variance of the side length
are printed below. The histogram shows their distribution, with a dashed line at
the 64 px training size.

```{r}
# 3.0.1  Native crop side lengths (square crops, so side = height = width). Cached.
side_cache <- here("analyses", "09_image_entropy", "entropy_cache", "side_lengths.rds")
if (file.exists(side_cache)) {
  side_lengths <- readRDS(side_cache)
} else {
  side_files <- list.files(data_dir,
    pattern = "\\.tif$", recursive = TRUE,
    full.names = TRUE
  )
  side_lengths <- vapply(
    side_files,
    function(f) dim(readTIFF(f, info = FALSE))[1], integer(1)
  )
  saveRDS(side_lengths, side_cache)
}
cat(sprintf(
  paste0(
    "Native crop side length (px): min = %d, median = %g, max = %d, ",
    "mean = %.1f, variance = %.1f (n = %d)\n"
  ),
  min(side_lengths), median(side_lengths), max(side_lengths),
  mean(side_lengths), var(side_lengths), length(side_lengths)
))
```

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
# 3.0.2  Histogram of native crop side lengths
p_sides <- ggplot(data.frame(side = side_lengths), aes(x = side)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 20, fill = "grey60", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 64, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#2166AC") +
  labs(x = "Native cropped-image side length (pixels)", y = "Number of CDAs") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 13), axis.title = element_text(size = 15))
p_sides
save_plot(p_sides, "crop_side_lengths.png", width = 8, height = 4.5, dir = "thesis_plots")
```

### 3.0.3 Example smallest and largest native crops

The five smallest and five largest original crops, all shown at the same size
with their median score and true side length. They are enlarged by
nearest-neighbour scaling, so the smallest look pixelated. The smallest crops are
tiny bounding boxes, mostly scored 0 or 1, over mostly healthy leaf. That is why
they look like noise. The largest each hold a whole CDA. Section 3.0.4 shows the
smallest boxes in context.

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=4.8}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.8
# 3.0.3
crop_panel <- function(f, side) {
  img <- readTIFF(f, info = FALSE)
  # Crops are foldered by median severity score (see the config chunk), so the
  # parent directory name is the score.
  score <- basename(dirname(f))
  ggplot() +
    annotation_raster(as.raster(img),
      xmin = 0, xmax = 1, ymin = 0, ymax = 1, interpolate = FALSE
    ) +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = sprintf("score %s, %d px", score, side)) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12))
}

crop_order <- order(side_lengths)
crop_sel <- c(head(crop_order, 5), tail(crop_order, 5))
example_panels <- lapply(crop_sel, function(i) {
  crop_panel(names(side_lengths)[i], side_lengths[i])
})

p_examples <- wrap_plots(example_panels, nrow = 2)
p_examples
save_plot(p_examples, "example_crops_min_max.png", width = 10, height = 4.8)
```

### 3.0.4 Smallest crops shown in context

The 20 smallest crops, each shown as a 200 × 200 px window of the original source
image. Each window is centred on the CDA's representative bounding box
(Medoid_Coords), outlined in cyan. This shows what each small box encloses. Many
of the smallest boxes sit on mostly healthy leaf and do not clearly enclose a cell
death area. They are probably annotation errors.

```{r fig.width=13, fig.height=11}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 11
# 3.0.4
context_csv <- read_csv(
  here(
    "analyses", "01_generate_raw_data", "04_representative_bounding_box_and_score",
    "combined_cda_data_medoid.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
context_csv_stem <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(context_csv$Basename)

# 200 x 200 px window from the native (rotated) source image, centred on the
# CDA's representative (Medoid_Coords) bounding box, outlined in cyan. Basenames
# are matched on their extension-stripped stem because the crop file name drops
# the original extension and does not preserve its case (.tif vs .TIF).
context_panel <- function(crop_path, side, half = 100) {
  fn <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(crop_path))
  m <- regmatches(fn, regexec("^(.*)_([0-9]+)_([0-9]+)_([0-9]+)$", fn))[[1]]
  base <- m[2]
  rr <- as.integer(m[3])
  cc <- as.integer(m[4])
  pp <- as.integer(m[5])
  r <- context_csv[
    context_csv_stem == base & context_csv$Row == rr &
      context_csv$Col == cc & context_csv$Pos == pp,
  ]
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  ci <- as.integer(r$Medoid_Coords)
  x1 <- as.integer(r[[paste0("X1_", ci)]])
  x2 <- as.integer(r[[paste0("X2_", ci)]])
  y1 <- as.integer(r[[paste0("Y1_", ci)]])
  y2 <- as.integer(r[[paste0("Y2_", ci)]])
  score <- basename(dirname(crop_path))
  img <- readTIFF(here("data", "raw_images_rotated", r$Basename[1]), info = FALSE)
  h_img <- dim(img)[1]
  w_img <- dim(img)[2]
  cx <- (x1 + x2) / 2
  cy <- (y1 + y2) / 2
  wx1 <- max(1, round(cx - half))
  wx2 <- min(w_img, round(cx + half))
  wy1 <- max(1, round(cy - half))
  wy2 <- min(h_img, round(cy + half))
  win <- img[wy1:wy2, wx1:wx2, ]
  wh <- dim(win)[1]
  ww <- dim(win)[2]
  ggplot() +
    annotation_raster(as.raster(win), 0, ww, 0, wh, interpolate = FALSE) +
    annotate("rect",
      xmin = x1 - wx1 + 1, xmax = x2 - wx1 + 1,
      ymin = wh - (y2 - wy1 + 1), ymax = wh - (y1 - wy1 + 1),
      fill = NA, colour = "cyan", linewidth = 0.9
    ) +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(0, ww), ylim = c(0, wh), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = sprintf("score %s, %d px", score, side)) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12))
}

context_sel <- head(order(side_lengths), 20)
context_panels <- lapply(context_sel, function(i) {
  context_panel(names(side_lengths)[i], side_lengths[i])
})
p_context <- wrap_plots(context_panels, nrow = 4)
p_context
save_plot(p_context, "smallest_crops_in_context.png", width = 13, height = 11)
```

### 3.1 Entropy across image sizes (parallel coordinates)

Each faint line is one CDA. It traces the CDA's Shannon entropy as the image
shrinks from the raw crop to 4 × 4 px. The thick line is the median at each size.
Entropy is almost flat from the raw crop down to 32 px. It dips slightly at 16 px
and falls sharply at 8 and 4 px, where the images are too small to hold their
range of values. 64 × 64 px is well within the flat region.

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
# 3.1
size_median <- metrics %>%
  group_by(size) %>%
  summarise(entropy = median(entropy), .groups = "drop")

p_parallel <- ggplot(metrics, aes(x = size, y = entropy)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = image_id), alpha = 0.03, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(
    data = size_median, aes(group = 1), colour = "#2166AC",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_point(data = size_median, colour = "#2166AC", size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "CDA image side length in pixels", y = "Shannon entropy") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text  = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15)
  )
p_parallel
save_plot(p_parallel, "parallel_coords.png",
  width = 8, height = 5,
  dir = "thesis_plots"
)
```

### 3.2 Entropy distribution at each image size (ridge plot)

The same information as stacked density curves, from the raw crop at the top to
4 × 4 px at the bottom. The distribution keeps its shape and position down to
16 px. At 8 and 4 px it shifts left and collapses.

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
# 3.2
# Manual ridgeline (the ggridges package is not available in this environment):
# a scaled kernel density per size, offset vertically by its row. The height
# factor is kept below 1 so each ridge stays clear of the next row's baseline,
# where the blue median markers sit - otherwise the ridge below rises over them.
# Raw is drawn at the top.
ridge_levels <- rev(size_levels) # 4 (bottom) ... Raw (top)
x_grid <- seq(min(metrics$entropy) - 0.3, max(metrics$entropy) + 0.3,
  length.out = 512
)

ridge_df <- metrics %>%
  group_by(size) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    d <- density(.x$entropy, from = min(x_grid), to = max(x_grid), n = 512)
    tibble(x = d$x, dens = d$y)
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(size) %>%
  mutate(dens = dens / max(dens)) %>% # normalise each ridge to unit height
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    row = match(as.character(size), ridge_levels) - 1,
    scale = 0.9, # height factor (<1 keeps each ridge below the next baseline)
    ymin = row,
    ymax = row + scale * dens
  )

# Median entropy per size, placed on each ridge's baseline and joined into a line
# in row (size) order via geom_path so the leftward shift at small sizes is
# visible directly on the ridges.
median_df <- metrics %>%
  group_by(size) %>%
  summarise(med_ent = median(entropy), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(row = match(as.character(size), ridge_levels) - 1)

p_ridge <- ggplot(ridge_df, aes(group = size)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = x, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
    fill = "grey75",
    colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(aes(x = x, y = ymax), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_path(
    data = median_df, aes(x = med_ent, y = row, group = 1),
    colour = "#2166AC", linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = median_df, aes(x = med_ent, y = row),
    shape = 21, fill = "#2166AC", colour = "white", stroke = 0.7, size = 2.4
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq_along(ridge_levels) - 1,
    labels = ridge_levels
  ) +
  labs(x = "Shannon entropy", y = "CDA image side length in pixels") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text  = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank()
  )
p_ridge
save_plot(p_ridge, "ridge_plot.png", width = 8, height = 5, dir = "thesis_plots")
```

### 3.3 Fraction of raw entropy retained at each size

A numerical summary of the two plots above. It gives the median entropy at each
size and the fraction of the raw median that remains. 64 × 64 px keeps almost all
the raw information. The loss only becomes large below 16 px.

```{r}
# 3.3
raw_median <- size_median$entropy[size_median$size == "Raw"]
size_median %>%
  mutate(fraction_of_raw = entropy / raw_median) %>%
  arrange(factor(size, levels = size_levels)) %>%
  mutate(
    entropy = round(entropy, 3),
    fraction_of_raw = round(fraction_of_raw, 3)
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

## 4. Image information versus severity score

### 4.1 Shannon entropy by score

Entropy of the raw crop against severity score. Entropy rises slightly with
score but overlaps heavily between adjacent scores. As the Year 1 review found,
Shannon entropy alone does not separate the severity scores cleanly.

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
# 4.1
p_ent_score <- ggplot(per_image, aes(x = score_f, y = entropy_raw)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = score_f), outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.18, height = 0, alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = "Severity Score", values = sev_pal) +
  labs(x = "Severity score", y = "Shannon entropy") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text    = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title   = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 11)
  )
p_ent_score
save_plot(p_ent_score, "entropy_score_boxplots.png", width = 8, height = 5)
```

## 5. Colour versus severity score

### 5.1 Green/red ratio by score

The log of the ratio of green to red pixels rises steadily with severity score.
This fits with cell death shifting the fluorescence from red, in healthy tissue,
towards green.

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
# 5.1
p_ratio <- ggplot(per_image, aes(x = score_f, y = log_gr)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = score_f), outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.18, height = 0, alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = "Severity Score", values = sev_pal) +
  labs(x = "Severity score", y = "log(Green / Red ratio)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text    = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title   = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 11)
  )
p_ratio
save_plot(p_ratio, "ratio_score_boxplots.png", width = 8, height = 5)
```

### 5.3 Mean green level by project

A CDA's green level depends on its severity, and also on the lighting and
exposure of its source image. These vary between imaging sessions and between
projects. Each point here is one CDA, and the boxes group CDAs by project, in
order of median green. The differences in green between projects come from
lighting, not from score.

```{r}
# 5.3.1
# Map each CDA to its source image and project. The cropped filenames are
# formatted <Basename>_<Row>_<Col>_<Pos>.tif, so stripping the trailing
# _Row_Col_Pos recovers the source-image basename (same approach as
# 07_visual_complexity). image_info.csv records the source Path once per folder
# (filled downwards); the top-level folder is the project, anonymised via the
# shared key.
image_info <- read_csv(
  here("analyses", "01_generate_raw_data", "01_allocation_info", "image_info.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  fill(Path) %>%
  mutate(
    Project = str_split_fixed(Path, "/", 2)[, 1],
    stem = str_remove(Image, "[.](tif|TIF)$")
  )

project_key <- read_csv(
  here("anonymisation_keys", "project_anonymisation_key.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
project_lut <- setNames(project_key$Anon_Label, project_key$Project)
stem_to_project <- setNames(project_lut[image_info$Project], image_info$stem)

per_image <- per_image %>%
  mutate(
    source  = str_remove(image_id, "_[0-9]+_[0-9]+_[0-9]+$"),
    project = unname(stem_to_project[source])
  )

n_unmapped <- sum(is.na(per_image$project))
cat(sprintf(
  "CDAs: %d | source images: %d | projects: %d | unmapped: %d\n",
  nrow(per_image), n_distinct(per_image$source),
  n_distinct(per_image$project), n_unmapped
))
```

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
# 5.3.2
project_order <- per_image %>%
  group_by(project) %>%
  summarise(med = median(mean_green), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(med) %>%
  pull(project)

p_green_proj <- per_image %>%
  mutate(project = factor(project, levels = project_order)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = project, y = mean_green)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = project), outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.18, height = 0, alpha = 0.12, size = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1", guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Project", y = "Mean green intensity (0-255)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text  = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15)
  )
p_green_proj
save_plot(p_green_proj, "green_project_boxplots.png", width = 8, height = 5)
```

### 5.4 Lighting-normalised green level by score

To remove the lighting difference between projects seen in §5.3, each CDA's
green level is centred on its project's mean and moved back to the overall mean
(`green_norm = green - project_mean + global_mean`). This corrects for each
project's brightness and keeps the score differences *within* each project. The
two panels below compare raw and corrected green by score.

The correction is made per project, not per source image. One source image holds
only about 30 CDAs, and their scores are correlated. So its mean green partly
depends on score, and correcting per image would remove real differences between
scores (see η² below). A project covers many source images and the full range of
scores, so its mean is a cleaner estimate of the lighting.

```{r fig.width=11, fig.height=5}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5
# 5.4.1
global_mean_green <- mean(per_image$mean_green)

per_image <- per_image %>%
  group_by(project) %>%
  mutate(green_norm = mean_green - mean(mean_green) + global_mean_green) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  mutate(green_norm_source = mean_green - mean(mean_green) + global_mean_green) %>%
  ungroup()

# eta^2: fraction of green variance explained by score. Higher = scores more
# separable. Compared across raw green and the two normalisation levels.
eta_sq <- function(y, g) {
  grand <- mean(y)
  ss_between <- sum(tapply(y, g, function(v) length(v) * (mean(v) - grand)^2))
  ss_between / sum((y - grand)^2)
}
cat(sprintf(
  "eta^2 (green ~ score):  raw = %.3f | project-normalised = %.3f | source-normalised = %.3f\n",
  eta_sq(per_image$mean_green, per_image$score),
  eta_sq(per_image$green_norm, per_image$score),
  eta_sq(per_image$green_norm_source, per_image$score)
))
cat(sprintf(
  "eta^2 (green ~ project): %.3f  (share of green variance that is between-project)\n",
  eta_sq(per_image$mean_green, per_image$project)
))

green_panel <- function(yvar, title) {
  ggplot(per_image, aes(x = score_f, y = .data[[yvar]])) +
    geom_boxplot(aes(fill = score_f), outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.18, height = 0, alpha = 0.12, size = 0.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(name = "Severity Score", values = sev_pal) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = range(c(per_image$mean_green, per_image$green_norm))) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Severity score", y = "Mean green intensity (0-255)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(size = 12), axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14)
    )
}

green_norm_raw <- green_panel("mean_green", "Raw")
green_norm_proj <- green_panel("green_norm", "Project-normalised")
p_green_norm <- (green_norm_raw | green_norm_proj) + plot_layout(guides = "collect")
p_green_norm
save_plot(p_green_norm, "green_score_normalised_boxplots.png", width = 11, height = 5)
```

### 5.5 Isolating the leaf region to estimate lighting

The correction in §5.4 uses green to estimate the lighting, which is circular.
A cleaner measure of lighting is the **brightness** of the leaf itself, the mean
of the red, green and blue channels. It is measured over leaf pixels only, so
the black background does not pull it down. The background includes holes and
gaps left by cell death at the leaf edge.

Two thresholds on each CDA's brightness histogram are compared for deciding which
pixels are leaf:

- **Otsu.** A threshold set for each image to maximise the variance between the
  two classes. It finds the natural split in the brightness distribution.
- **Leaf (background only).** A low fixed threshold, brightness ≥ 0.1. It removes
  only the near-black background and keeps *all* the tissue.

Otsu removes the black background cleanly where there is one. But healthy tissue
fluoresces darker red, and lesions are bright yellow-green. So in CDAs with higher
scores, Otsu picks out the **lesion** rather than the whole leaf. Its brightness
then follows the score, which makes it a poor measure of lighting. The
background-only leaf brightness does not follow the score. Example masks, one CDA
per score, are in the segmentation analysis (`10_segmentation_and_feature_extraction`,
§3.2).

```{r}
# 5.5.2
# eta^2 (~ score) quantifies how much each brightness measure is driven by score
# rather than lighting. A good lighting proxy should be LOW.
cat(sprintf(
  "eta^2 (~ score):  Otsu brightness = %.3f  |  leaf brightness = %.3f\n",
  eta_sq(per_image$otsu_bright, per_image$score),
  eta_sq(per_image$leaf_bright, per_image$score)
))
cat(sprintf(
  "eta^2 (~ project): leaf brightness = %.3f  (more between-project variation than green's %.3f)\n",
  eta_sq(per_image$leaf_bright, per_image$project),
  eta_sq(per_image$mean_green, per_image$project)
))
```

Leaf brightness depends much less on score than Otsu brightness does. It also
varies more between projects than green does, which is the lighting variation.
So it is used as the measure of lighting. Grouped by project, it shows the same
lighting differences as green in §5.3.

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
# 5.5.3
lb_order <- per_image %>%
  group_by(project) %>%
  summarise(med = median(leaf_bright), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(med) %>%
  pull(project)

p_leafbright_proj <- per_image %>%
  mutate(project = factor(project, levels = lb_order)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = project, y = leaf_bright)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = project), outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.18, height = 0, alpha = 0.12, size = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1", guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Project", y = "Mean leaf brightness (0-255)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 13), axis.title = element_text(size = 15))
p_leafbright_proj
save_plot(p_leafbright_proj, "leaf_brightness_project_boxplots.png", width = 8, height = 5)
```

### 5.6 Normalising green by leaf brightness

Each CDA's green is now divided by the leaf brightness of its source image, or of
its project, and scaled to the overall mean. This corrects for the lighting of
each source image or project by multiplication. Unlike §5.4, it does not use
green to estimate the lighting. The panels compare raw green with the best
correction, which is per source image.

```{r fig.width=11, fig.height=5}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5
# 5.6.1
global_leaf <- mean(per_image$leaf_bright)

per_image <- per_image %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  mutate(green_lb_source = mean_green * global_leaf / mean(leaf_bright)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(project) %>%
  mutate(green_lb_project = mean_green * global_leaf / mean(leaf_bright)) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("eta^2 (green ~ score), higher = more separable:\n")
cat(sprintf("  raw green                          = %.3f\n", eta_sq(per_image$mean_green, per_image$score)))
cat(sprintf("  green-mean normalised (project, 5.4) = %.3f\n", eta_sq(per_image$green_norm, per_image$score)))
cat(sprintf("  leaf-brightness normalised (project) = %.3f\n", eta_sq(per_image$green_lb_project, per_image$score)))
cat(sprintf("  leaf-brightness normalised (source)  = %.3f\n", eta_sq(per_image$green_lb_source, per_image$score)))

green_panel2 <- function(yvar, title) {
  ggplot(per_image, aes(x = score_f, y = .data[[yvar]])) +
    geom_boxplot(aes(fill = score_f), outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.18, height = 0, alpha = 0.12, size = 0.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(name = "Severity Score", values = sev_pal) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = range(c(per_image$mean_green, per_image$green_lb_source))) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Severity score", y = "Mean green intensity (0-255)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(size = 12), axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14)
    )
}

green_lb_raw <- green_panel2("mean_green", "Raw")
green_lb_norm <- green_panel2("green_lb_source", "Leaf-brightness normalised (per source)")
p_green_lb <- (green_lb_raw | green_lb_norm) + plot_layout(guides = "collect")
p_green_lb
save_plot(p_green_lb, "green_score_leafnorm_boxplots.png", width = 11, height = 5)
```

Correcting green for leaf brightness improves it more than any other correction
tried (η² ≈ 0.52 → 0.58). This confirms that lighting differences between source
images add real noise. But the gain is small, and the boxes for adjacent scores
still overlap heavily. Even the best single hand-crafted feature, corrected for
lighting, cannot separate neighbouring scores. This is why a learned model is
used (see `07_visual_complexity`) rather than hand-crafted features.

### 5.7 Green/red ratio versus entropy

The Year 1 review also asked whether entropy and colour carry the same
information. They do not. The green to red ratio and Shannon entropy are only
weakly related. So colour separates the scores (§5.1) where entropy alone does
not (§4.1).

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
# 5.7
r_gr_ent <- cor(per_image$log_gr, per_image$entropy_raw)

p_scatter <- ggplot(per_image, aes(x = entropy_raw, y = log_gr)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = score_f), alpha = 0.3, size = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = "Severity Score", values = sev_pal) +
  labs(
    x = "Shannon entropy", y = "log(Green / Red ratio)",
    subtitle = sprintf("Pearson r = %.2f", r_gr_ent)
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, size = 2))) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text    = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title   = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 11)
  )
p_scatter
save_plot(p_scatter, "ratio_entropy_scatter.png", width = 8, height = 5)
```

---

## 6. Interpretation and Discussion

- **Input size.** Shannon entropy holds from the raw crop down to about 16 px.
  It only falls sharply at 8 and 4 px (§3.1 to 3.3). So 64 × 64 px keeps almost
  all the information in the raw crops with few pixels and little training
  compute. This supports the 64 × 64 input size used for training (see
  `07_visual_complexity`).
- **Entropy and score.** Entropy overlaps heavily between adjacent scores
  (§4.1). It cannot classify severity on its own.
- **Colour and score.** The green to red ratio (§5.1) and the mean green level
  (§5.2) both rise steadily with severity. Colour is only weakly correlated with
  entropy (§5.7). So colour carries information about score that entropy does
  not.
- **Lighting is a real confound that can only partly be removed.** Green level
  varies between projects (§5.3). About 16% of the variance in green lies
  between projects. This confirms that imaging and lighting differences add
  noise on top of the differences between scores. Three corrections were tried:
  - *Centring green on the project mean* (§5.4). This removes the offset and
    slightly narrows the spread within each score. The gain is small, because a
    CDA's green partly depends on which project it is from.
  - *Centring on each source image* (§5.4). This over-corrects. A source image's
    mean green partly depends on the scores of its roughly 30 CDAs, so the
    correction removes real differences.
  - *Segmenting the leaf and dividing green by leaf brightness* (§5.5 and 5.6).
    This is the best measure of lighting. Leaf brightness depends much less on
    score than Otsu brightness, which picks out the lesion. It also varies more
    between projects than green. This gives the largest improvement
    (η² ≈ 0.52 → 0.58).
- **The features are not enough.** Even the best single feature, corrected for
  lighting, leaves neighbouring scores overlapping heavily (§5.6). Hand-crafted
  colour, brightness and entropy features capture part of what determines
  severity. They cannot cleanly separate adjacent scores, which is why a learned
  model is used instead.
```
